title: Adaptive Filtering with Reinforcement Learning against Model Mismatch in Low-Observable Settings

problem.claim: Estimating the states of dynamical systems is important across numerous applications.

gap.claim: Existing subspace identification methods for mismatched models assume fully observable systems, leaving low-observable settings unaddressed.

narrative_sequence.summary: State estimation of dynamical systems is presented as a central problem.
Optimal solutions are established for completely known system dynamics, including the Kalman filter in the linear–Gaussian setting.
Under model mismatch, subspace identification methods are commonly used but require fully observable systems.

source_observation.claim: Subspace identification methods for model-mismatched systems assume full observability.

interpretation.claim: Reduced observability is a material boundary condition for applying these methods.

application.claim: When adapting state-estimation methods, explicitly test whether their observability assumptions hold.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish how such methods behave outside fully observable systems.

unknowns: The supplied units do not describe the paper's proposed method.
The supplied units do not report experiments, datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The supplied units do not establish an explicitly claimed novel contribution.
